extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies and regulators preparing state plans under CAA section 111, affected EGU operators, and reliability authorities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for states on invoking Remaining Useful Life or Other Factors (RULOF) to apply less-stringent standards of performance or longer compliance schedules for particular affected EGUs, including required analyses, evidence, evaluation of control options, expression of standards, increments of progress, and reliability demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for longer compliance schedule notwithstanding best efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: States should show that the need to provide a longer compliance schedule is notwithstanding best efforts on the parts of all relevant parties to achieve timely compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA expects documentation demonstrating that delays were due to circumstances outside the control of the state and affected EGU and not caused by self-created circumstances. Helpful evidence includes permits, contracts, receipts, invoices, and correspondence with vendors and regulators. States may still reasonably justify a longer schedule based on other types of information or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of performance must be no less stringent than necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: If a state demonstrates an affected EGU cannot reasonably achieve the applicable degree of emission limitation, it may apply a less stringent standard or longer schedule, but the standard must be no less stringent than necessary to address the fundamental difference and as close to the EPA's degree of emission limitation or schedule as reasonably possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to 40 CFR 60.24a(f), the state must determine the degree of emission limitation the EGU can reasonably achieve and use that degree as the basis for the source-specific standard. Example: if 88.4% reduction is infeasible for a unit but 85% capture is achievable, the state may set a standard corresponding to 85% capture if no other system can achieve 88.4%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate systems of emission reduction to the extent necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: States must evaluate, to the extent necessary, the systems of emission reduction the EPA identified in the applicable emission guidelines using the factors and evaluation metrics the Agency considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA anticipates states will leverage EPA-provided information and other technical, cost, and related record materials and particularize them to individual EGUs. It will often not be necessary to consider all systems identified; evaluation should be limited to what is needed to determine a standard as close as reasonably possible to the presumptive standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of additional systems beyond EPA-identified options
rubrics_metrics.description: States may consider additional systems of emission reduction that the EPA did not identify but that the state believes are available and may be reasonable for a particular affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This flexibility is provided by the general implementing regulations and allows states to identify other reasonable technology or system approaches specific to a facility’s circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not re-evaluate systems already shown infeasible
rubrics_metrics.description: If a state has already determined under 40 CFR 60.24a(e) that a particular system is not reasonably possible for an affected EGU, the state does not need to evaluate that system again when determining a less stringent standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, if evaluating the most stringent feasible system demonstrates implementability, further evaluation of other systems may not be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: For systems with ranges, start with most stringent feasible iteration
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems of emission reduction that have a range of potential stringencies, states should start by evaluating the most stringent iteration that is potentially feasible for the particular affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If that stringency is not reasonable, the state should evaluate lower stringencies as needed until identifying the standard that is no less stringent than necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation factors and metrics required
rubrics_metrics.description: In evaluating systems of emission reduction, states must consider the factors and evaluation metrics the EPA considered: technical feasibility, the amount of emission reductions, any non-air quality health and environmental impacts, and energy requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may also consider other facility-specific factors that constitute a fundamental difference between EPA's information and the particular affected EGU circumstances (e.g., remote location making pipeline construction infeasible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression of source-specific standard as rate-based emission limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any less stringent standard of performance applied pursuant to RULOF must be determined and expressed in the form of a rate-based emission limitation (lb CO2/MWh).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the source-specific standard is no less stringent than the EPA's presumptive rate-based standard. EPA is not providing that RULOF-based standards can use mass-based or rate-based compliance flexibilities under these emission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance schedule length must be no longer than necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: A longer compliance schedule pursuant to RULOF must be no longer than necessary to address the fundamental difference identified under 40 CFR 60.24a(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For states applying less-stringent standards based on a system other than the BSER, the compliance schedule should be consistent with installation and implementation of that system and be as expeditious as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legally enforceable increments of progress when schedule exceeds threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Any compliance schedule extending more than twenty months past the state plan submission deadline must include legally enforceable increments of progress (IoPs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under these emission guidelines (24-month plan submission deadline and compliance dates beyond that), IoPs are required for BSERs that involve installation of emissions controls (long-term and medium-term coal-fired EGUs). IoPs provide checkpoints and transparency for long construction and installation timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: IoPs must be tailored to BSER or correspond to 40 CFR 60.21a(h) steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Units complying through the BSER specified for each subcategory must use IoPs tailored to those BSERs. Units complying through a different control technology must adopt increments corresponding to each step in 40 CFR 60.21a(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each increment must have a calendar date deadline; states have discretion to set dates based on unit circumstances. EPA is finalizing exemption of natural gas- and oil-fired subcategories from IoP requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency requirements for operating-condition-based RULOF
rubrics_metrics.description: If a state invokes RULOF based on an operating condition within the control of an affected EGU (e.g., remaining useful life or specific utilization level), the state plan must include such operating condition(s) as an enforceable requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans must include provisions for implementation and enforcement of the operating conditions, including monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping. States may revise plans if circumstances change after plan submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optionality on enforceable retirement dates and operating restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: States are not required by these emission guidelines to impose enforceable retirement dates or operating restrictions on affected EGUs; it is within the state's discretion whether such requirements are appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a state determines such enforceable commitments are appropriate, those considerations can form the basis for applying a less stringent standard under subpart Ba.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term coal-fired EGU evaluation order and options
rubrics_metrics.description: For long-term coal-fired steam generating EGUs, EPA identified CCS with 90% capture, CCS with lower capture rates, natural gas co-firing, and HRI as potential systems. If a unit can install CCS but cannot achieve 88.4% reduction, the state should evaluate CCS with lower capture rates; if CCS is infeasible, evaluate co-firing and then HRI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State should identify the most stringent degree achievable by CCS (or other system) and use that as the less-stringent standard if no other system can meet the presumptive standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium-term coal-fired EGU evaluation approach
rubrics_metrics.description: For medium-term coal-fired steam generating EGUs, EPA identified CCS, natural gas co-firing, and HRI, but believes CCS cost-effectiveness is less favorable; states may reasonably forgo evaluating CCS and should start by evaluating natural gas co-firing (beginning at 40%), then lower levels, and then HRI if co-firing is infeasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should demonstrate under 40 CFR 60.24a(e) if natural gas co-firing is infeasible for a particular unit before moving to HRI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation that sources can implement some emission-reduction measures
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA expects that any coal-fired steam generating EGU to which a less-stringent standard is applied will be able to reasonably implement some system of emission reduction; at a minimum, sources should be able to institute approaches to maintain their historical heat rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This serves as a baseline expectation that some mitigation or efficiency measures remain available even if major controls are infeasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF-based standards must meet all other applicable requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any less-stringent standard of performance under RULOF must meet all other applicable requirements of both the general implementing regulations and these emission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should ensure compliance with 40 CFR part 60 subpart Ba requirements in addition to the specific RULOF determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and documentation requirements to justify longer schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: To use RULOF to extend schedules beyond the 1-year extension mechanism, the state must provide documentation showing the need for a longer schedule was due to circumstances outside the affected EGU's control and that the affected EGU met relevant increments of progress and obligations timely prior to the delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helpful documentation includes permits, contracts, receipts, invoices, and vendor/regulator correspondence. The state must also demonstrate the revised schedule is no longer than necessary to accommodate the delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability-related RULOF demonstration elements
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply RULOF based on unit-specific reliability considerations, a state must demonstrate a fundamental difference between EPA's reliability information and the unit's circumstances, showing that requiring compliance by the compliance date would compromise reliability (e.g., necessitate taking the unit offline causing resource adequacy shortfall).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis must clearly demonstrate the unit is reliability-critical such that compliance would trigger non-compliance with mandatory FERC-approved reliability standards or increase loss of load expectation beyond regional targets. The analysis must include a projection of the period the unit is expected to be reliability critical and corroboration from the relevant reliability Planning Authority, including a certification that the identified reliability problem exists and requires the requested relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for Planning Authority corroboration and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans seeking RULOF relief for reliability must include analysis by the relevant Planning Authority that corroborates the asserted reliability risk and confirms the period the unit is projected to be reliability-critical, plus a certification from the Planning Authority that the claims are accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement ensures independent verification that the designated unit is needed for resource adequacy and that compliance would interfere with that function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic reliability claims are insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: A generic or unsubstantiated reliability or resource adequacy concern is not sufficient to substantiate a fundamental difference or to justify RULOF relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must provide specific, documented demonstrations (including Planning Authority corroboration) showing the unit-specific nature of the reliability problem; mere assertions that grid reliability is a concern will not suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of temporary compliance date extension mechanism before RULOF
rubrics_metrics.description: States may include a mechanism in plans to provide a compliance deadline extension of up to 1 year for certain affected EGUs with add-on control technologies when the extension is needed due to circumstances outside the affected EGU's control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the state and EGU believe 1 year is insufficient, the state may begin a plan revision and use RULOF to seek a longer schedule, but must demonstrate a fundamental difference, provide documentation, and show the delay was not self-created and that progress had been timely up to the delay.
